notes: Built over the grave of Sugawara no Michizane; a head shrine of the Tenjin faith.

details.history: Founded in 919 over the tomb of Sugawara no Michizane, the Heian scholar-statesman who died in exile at Dazaifu in 903. After misfortunes struck the capital, he was deified as Tenjin, the kami of learning.
details.why_visit: The spiritual home of students across Japan, who come to pray for academic success; the grounds are famed for some 6,000 plum trees that bloom in late winter.
details.prayer_focus: Academic achievement (学業成就) and success in examinations (合格祈願), petitioned on ema and at the bronze ox statues.
details.best_season: Late February to March for the plum blossoms (Michizane's beloved flower); examination season draws the largest crowds.

deities.role: Enshrined as Tenjin (主祭神), the kami of scholarship.
deities.regional_lore: Slandered and exiled from the court to Dazaifu, Michizane died here in 903. A series of plagues and lightning strikes on the capital were attributed to his vengeful spirit, who was pacified and enshrined as Tenman-Tenjin; over time the storm-god of grievance became the gentle patron of learning.

canonical.title: Heian-era scholar and statesman (845–903), deified as Tenjin
canonical.canonical_lore: A renowned poet and minister of the Heian court, later venerated nationwide as the kami of academics.

events.time_prose: Late September, over several days around the autumnal equinox.
events.origin: The shrine's principal annual festival, re-enacting the consolation of Michizane's spirit.
events.meaning: To comfort the enshrined kami and pray for peace and learning.
events.ritual: A grand procession bears the divine palanquin (o-mikoshi) through the town in Heian-style costume.
events.prayer: For scholarship, and for the repose and favor of Tenjin.
events.visitor_notes: The costumed evening procession is the highlight; the approach fills with festival stalls.

deities.role: Honored kami borne in the procession
